newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian diamond miner may seek foreign partner.
newsitem.headline: Russian diamond miner may seek foreign partner.

text.p: A Russian diamond mining company said on Monday that it may consider inviting foreign miners to help tap the large Lomonosov diamond field near the northern port city of Arkhangelsk.
"We are considering all options (for a development partnership) right now, both domestic and foreign," said Vitaly Fortygin, general director of Severalmaz, which holds the license to tap Lomonosov.
Fortygin, speaking from Arkhangelsk, said Severalmaz was considering working with Eastern Mining Ltd, RTZ Corp Plc, CRA Ltd and De Beers, among others.
He said Severalmaz aimed to begin mining operations in 1999 after exploration work and a two-year feasiblity were completed and that Lomonosov could be worth $12 billion.
Foreign companies have projects to mine Russian precious metals like gold, but there are no deals up and running for outside companies to tap gems.
The State Duma lower house of parliament has said it opposes the participation of foreign companies in Russian gem mining.

But De Beers said in December 1996 that it had signed a deal with Russian mining company Terra to set up a diamond exploration joint venture for gem fields adjacent to Lomonosov in the Arkhangelsk region.
Severalmaz has a deal to send all rough gems mined during exploration at Lomonosov to the Kristall gem cutting factory.

Severalmaz, whose biggest shareholders include the Arkhangelsk Regional Property Committee (over 25 percent), state oil holding company Rosneft (15 percent) and local exploration company Arkhangelskgeoldobycha (14 percent), was founded in 1992 and received a licence to tap Lomonosov in 1994.
